chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: Headed to Chicago by way of Kalamazoo
summary: Trummy announces the booking, Malachi has never been farther than New York, and the band breaks in for two weeks in Kalamazoo.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: One day Trummy walked in the rehearsal, and he told us about this gig that he had. As a matter of fact, the agent had been waiting for the band to rehearse and be ready before he booked us. So I guess Trummy must have called him and told him we was ready to move. And Trummy came to the rehearsal one day and said, "We're going to Chicago. But on the way to Chicago, we've got two weeks in Kalamazoo, Michigan, we'll play that, and then we'll go to Chicago." So never having... The furthest that I had been away from Washington at that particular time was New York, which was a short time when I think Osie, Tommy Potter, I think Charlie Rouse might have been with us when we went up just for a holiday sometime during the time we were working at the Caverns, I guess. But other than that, as far as places like Chicago and California, at that time they were places that were far, far away.

So that the idea of going to Chicago, much as I had heard about it... And that was from listening to Earl Hines at the Grand Terrace, listening to Roy Eldridge at...oh, I forgot the name of the place Roy Eldridge used to play in Chicago, but I think it was on Wabash Avenue. I used to get him sometimes at 3 or 4 o'clock in the morning from out there. The tune that I remember him playing most times was a thing called "Heckler's Hop." But that was about the extent of my knowing what
Chicago was all about, other than knowing about Al Capone and people like that. I knew it was the gangster capital of the world! Yeah, we were pretty excited about it.

So we boarded the train here one morning, headed for Kalamazoo, Michigan. We got there, and it was a nice place for us to break the band prior to going to Chicago, because a couple of weeks there, and the band got a chance to actually be exposed, and the audience was very... You know, everybody seemed to know Trummy Young at that particular time.
